articles.headline: Philadelphia Annual Conference (editorial review of the session)
articles.summary: The recent session of the Philadelphia Annual Conference exhibited marked improvement on the previous sessions of that body. The financial reports were promptly made, and but few of the brethren had to return to their Conference collections.
people: spoke; elected delegate to General Conference (Rev.)
member forty years; elected delegate to General Conference (Rev.)

articles.headline: Sad Bereavement (death of Mrs. Hollen)
articles.summary: The highly esteemed and Christian wife of Rev. James Hollen, late pastor of Bethel Church of this city, died last Tuesday afternoon. She died in peace with Jesus, and in full hope of a blissful immortality. We go to press before the funeral will take place.
people: husband of deceased; late pastor of Bethel Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Bishop Wayman Gone Southward
articles.summary: Bishop A. W. Wayman left this city Monday night last at 11 o'clock for Macon, Georgia, to hold the Georgia Conference, or rather to organize it. The Bishop is accompanied by Rev. R. P. Gibbs, formerly pastor of the Union Church, Philadelphia, who will take charge of the Union Church, Savannah, Ga., and also by Rev. A. T. Carr, of Georgetown, S. C.
people: formerly pastor of Union Church, Phila.; to Union Church, Savannah (Rev.)

articles.headline: Daughters of Conference
articles.summary: The daughters of Conference belonging to Bethel Church were addressed on Monday evening by Rev. Joshua Woodlin, of Brooklyn, in a sermon of great power. On Tuesday morning, Sisters Highgate and Rich, on behalf of the Daughters of Conference, presented to the ministers each a sum of money.

articles.headline: The Book Concern (Rev. Theodore Gould appointed travelling agent)
articles.summary: Rev. Theodore Gould has been appointed by Bishop Wayman and the Philadelphia Conference a travelling Agent for the Book Concern. Now let the brethren every where wake up.

articles.headline: Colored Militia in New Jersey (Sumner company, Camden)
articles.summary: A company of militia, composed of colored men, has been organized in Camden, of which Harrison Grinage, also a colored man, has been elected captain. Out of compliment to Senator Sumner, the company has been named after him. (Sumner letter, Washington, May 27, 1867, via Hon. J. M. Scovel; from the Phila. Press.)

articles.headline: Call and Get One (Conference group photograph)
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Annual Conference was photographed in group while holding its Annual Session. A number of copies of this fine picture have been struck off, and are for sale, at the A.M.E. Book Store 631 Pine St.

articles.headline: Rev. Stephen Smith's gift to the missionary society
articles.summary: Rev. R. H. Cain, Superintendent of Missions in South Carolina, in a letter to the Corresponding Secretary of the P. H. and F. Missionary Society, Rev. John M. Brown, said 'The people are coming into the A.M.E. Church in this State, not by hundreds, but by thousands.' On hearing this statement, Rev. Stephen Smith drew a check on Jay Cooke (Banker) for fifty dollars, payable to the order of the Corresponding Secretary.

articles.headline: In Memory of the Late Dr. James Mc. C. Crummill (Bensalem Equal Rights League)
articles.author: William B. Purvis
articles.summary: At a special meeting of the Mc. C. Crummill Equal Rights League, of Bensalem, the following preamble and resolutions were passed: Whereas, It has pleased Almighty God, in His divine providence, to remove from among us, our late friend and brother, James Mc. C. Crummill...

When I last heard from them they were in Washington. Please let it be known to Rev Jacob Mitchell. Address John Harrison Bean, Medford, Burlington county, New Jersey. In care of Robert Davis. articles.headline: Our Appointment (editor appointed to Bethel; wishes to go South)
articles.author: James Lynch
articles.summary: At the recent session of the Philadelphia Conference, we were appointed to the pastoral charge of Bethel Church of this city, in connection with the editorial control of the Christian Recorder. Notwithstanding the great amount of labor this double appointment would involve, we would attempt it with willingness and hope, did not our whole heart say, 'Go South!' ... on the eve of his leaving for Georgia we asked [Bishop Wayman] if there would be impropriety in tendering our resignation ... and he answered in the negative. We have not heard from him yet.

articles.headline: Valedictory (James Lynch resigns the editorship)
articles.author: James Lynch
articles.summary: To the Readers of the Christian Recorder.--It is with deep regret I announce my peremptory resignation of the Editorial control of the organ of the A. M. E. Church. ... For a little over sixteen months I have held the position. ... Between myself and the General Book Steward, who was formerly the editor, though he has steadily maintained the illegality of my appointment, which displaced him, there is the best of feeling ... They impel me to go to a Southern State, and unite my destiny with that of my people ... I hope that God will bless my colleague, Rev. Elisha Weaver, and that as the Travelling Agent, Rev. Theodore Gould, can perform most of the labor which devolved on Brother Weaver, I have no doubt that my avowed course will not prove prejudicial to the interests of the Book Concern. Stand by the Recorder. Friendly readers--Farewell! James Lynch, Editor of Christian Recorder.
people: General Book Steward, formerly the editor (Rev.)

articles.headline: Rev. James Lynch (Christian Advocate, New York, on the retiring editor)
articles.summary: The Christian Advocate, New York, notices Rev. James Lynch, the retiring editor of the Christian Recorder, as follows. The editorial management of the Christian Recorder, the organ of the African M. E. Church, now changes, the editor, Rev. James Lynch, having peremptorily resigned. The former editor, Rev. articles.headline: Correction (Excelsior Base Ball Club concert)
articles.author: Geo. H. Wilson [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor--In justice to our Association, I think that a little correction to an article in your last week's issue, relative to a concert given on the evening of the 28th ult. is highly necessary. Your correspondent errs when he says 'a beautiful silk flag was presented to Mr. Jas. articles.headline: Our Ex-Editor (Lynch commissioned by the Union Republican Congressional Committee for Mississippi)
articles.summary: We feel that our ex-editor, Rev. James Lynch will have his hands full at the South, as in addition to his missionary labor, he will act under the auspices of the Union Republican Congressional Committee. We have seen his commission ... (Washington, D.C., June 15th 1867, to Rev. James Lynch, Phila. Pa., to operate in the State of Mississippi, signed Thomas L. Tullock). This appointment was made mainly on the recommendation of Hon. W. D. Kelley, and prominent white citizens of Philadelphia ... arranged at a meeting of several Congressmen and Gov. Ward, at the Continental Hotel, about two weeks since.

events.name: Philadelphia A.M.E. Annual Conference, spring 1867 session (proceedings, second to fourth days)
events.location: Philadelphia (Bethel Church named for the Book Concern mass meeting)
events.description: 'For the Christian Recorder.' Second day: religious services by Rev. G. T. Waters; General Book Steward Rev. Elisha Weaver made his annual report (speaking of a financial panic); Rev. Stephen Smith objected to remarks before its reception; on motion of Jonathan Hamilton the report was received. Question 4th (preachers admitted on trial): J. P. B. Eddy moved that Thos. V. Pierce, a regularly ordained elder of the British Methodist Episcopal Church, be admitted; William Moore spoke for him; admitted. D. P. Seaton offered Frisby J. Cooper of Wilmington, Delaware, for local membership (admitted), and presented Isaac Parker, an ordained minister of the African Union Church. Benediction by Rev. B. Lynch. Third day: Bishop Wayman presiding; services by Rev. W. H. Williams; Stephen Smith moved that local preachers not attending by Wednesday 10 o'clock be fined $1; on motion of W. H. Williams money was appropriated to give Father Bulaugh (editorial prints Boulaugh), the oldest minister in the connection, immediate relief. Rev. Isaac Parker took the A.M.E. ordination vows and on motion of Stephen Smith was admitted. Jacob Mitchell offered Jacob Jay (laid over). T. A. Cuff of Reading offered Walter Thomson for the itinerancy and Samuel Underhill for local membership. Edward Lawe offered Joel Fisher for local membership (not admitted). H. J. Rhodes of West Philadelphia offered W. D. Johnson and George Washington. James Hollen offered Littleton Dennis and Benjamin Lloyd for local membership, then withdrew the applications to make corrections. William Williams of Lancaster offered Robert Boston; William H. Chase of Montrose offered Jacob Wilkeholm for the itinerancy; Isaiah S. Taylor of Delaware offered Peter Loper; R. P. Gibbs offered Ephraim Wilson, a local deacon from Zion A.M.E. Church (parchments approved, admitted). Rev. Dr. Taylor, corresponding secretary of the American Bible Society, and Mr. Jewell were introduced; Rev. John M. Brown responded; E. Weaver moved resolutions; committee on the Bible Cause: James Lynch, Stephen Smith, Elisha Weaver, W. Moore and Theodore Gould. The committee in the case of Joseph A. Nelson, charged by the Trustees of Germantown with fraud, found him guilty; James Lynch moved reconsideration, opposed by E. Weaver and H. J. Rhodes, lost; Lynch gave notice of a new trial. Committee on Temperance (chairman W. H. Chase) urged temperance societies in all charges. On motion of E. Weaver no church meetings Wednesday evening; all invited to the Book Concern mass meeting at Bethel Church. Benediction by Rev. Mr. Alston. Fourth day: Bishop Wayman presiding; services by Rev. George Thornton; on James Lynch's resolution a new investigation was granted Rev. Joseph Nelson, committee Jeremiah Young, J. V. Pierce, W. H. Williams, W. W. Grimes and T. A. Cuff. (To be continued.)

events.name: Book Concern mass meeting during the Philadelphia Annual Conference
events.description: Great mass meetings were held during the sitting of the Philadelphia Annual Conference. The one in behalf of the A.M.E. Book Concern was an immense gathering; Bethel Church was literally packed. Revs. James A. Shorter, Brown, Woodlin, Weaver, Lynch, and Messrs. Isaiah Wears and A. Fields spoke; a collection was lifted. The missionary meeting was likewise large: Rev. John M. Brown, the corresponding secretary, spoke; about $75.00 raised; $25 paid by friends to make Bishop A. W. Wayman a life member of the society.

events.name: Sabbath School anniversaries (Bethel, Wesley, Zion Mission, Camden, West Philadelphia; Union and Frankford)
events.description: The anniversary of the Sabbath Schools of Bethel, Wesley, Zion Mission, Camden and West Philadelphia took place at Bethel Church on Monday afternoon last; addresses by members of the Conference. The Union Church and Frankford Sabbath Schools held their anniversaries at Union Church on Tuesday afternoon (May 28); the young people in the northern part of the city, as in the southern, are waking up. No individuals named.

events.name: Grand Union Camp Meeting of the Philadelphia Conference (announced)

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference, fifth to ninth days (synopsis)
events.description: The new committee on Joseph A. Nelson's case (charged with fraud by the trustees of Germantown) found him perfectly innocent; money raised was paid out for repairs, mortgage, travelling expenses, salary and legal fees. Peter Loper, Walter Thompson and Jacob Wilsheim (printed 'Wilshelm'; earlier 'Wilkehelm') admitted to the itinerancy on trial; Littleton Dennis, Frisby J. Cooper, Samuel Underhill, Robert Boston and Benjamin Lloyd admitted to local conference membership on trial. Ephraim Wilson, a local deacon from Zion Church, admitted. W. H. Turner, H. H. Lewis and Benjamin Darks admitted into full connection. Committees on Book Concern, Education, Temperance and Sabbath-schools reported; a plan to relieve the Book Concern of its financial embarrassment. Jacob Jay, by vote of Conference, reprimanded severely by the Bishop. Conference pledged $500 for the Missionary Cause and a share of Bishop Payne's tour to England. Ordination of deacons. Vineland Circuit divided. Conference Stewards reported. Resolutions passed recommending the congregation of Wesley Church, Hurst street, to sell their building and move to the western part of the city. Report on Wilberforce University. $200 loaned by the Missionary Fund to the Book Concern at 6 per cent for one year. $125 paid to Rev. John M. Brown, Corresponding Secretary of the Parent Home and Foreign Missionary Society. Standing Committees and appointments announced (as published last week). The Annual Sermon preached by Rev. Peter Gardiner. Minutes delayed: 'We have had the Recorder to edit, Bethel Church to attend to, and the minutes to prepare.'

events.description: LOCAL: The Walker's Union League [name printed 'Waltke's'/'Walker's': VERIFY], a beneficial society of recent formation, held an important meeting on Tuesday last, to review the working condition of the Association and devise means for its future improvement; adjourned to September 3d. events.name: Trustees of the A.M.E. Book Concern -- accept Lynch's resignation; Weaver to fill the editorial chair
events.description: The Trustees of the A. M. E. Book Concern met, Philadelphia, June 13th, 1867. Present: Revs. Elisha Weaver, James Lynch, Stephen Smith, William Moore, N. H. Turpin, H. J. Rhodes (by proxy). Jacob Mitchell was not in the State. The resignation of Rev. James Lynch was considered; regret expressed, but he would not yield. The resignation was accepted and resolutions passed (his course highly honorable; thanks and prayers), signed Stephen Smith, William Moore, H. J. Rhodes, N. H. Turpin, Elisha Weaver, Chairman. Lynch responded with deep emotion. On motion of N. H. Turpin, it was resolved that Rev. Elisha Weaver fill the editorial chair. E. Weaver, Chairman of Book Committee.
attendees: chairman; named to fill the editorial chair (Rev.)

An address reviewing the history of the Association and urging the members to renewed activity was delivered by the President, Mr. Isaiah C.
